newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end volatile day up on soymeal gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end volatile day up on soymeal gains.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended a volatile session higher, lifted by strong gains in soymeal, pit sources said.
"I think we're just having an awful time breaking the meal market with the May on the board," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp.
Armstrong and others noted there had been no deliveries posted against the May soymeal and none were expected.
Technicals were also looking up. Many traders had said Monday's sharp losses indicated a key reversal but Tuesday's strong close may have renewed bullish interest.

"Technically it sold off early and went to the $8.60 (July) uptrend line and it held to a T," said Bill Biedermann of Allendale Corp. "The trendline came off the February and April lows and it held so we're still going up."

Soybeans were pressured near midday by news U.S. firm, Owensboro Grain Co. is negotiating to buy more soybeans from South America. The company would not confirm tonnage but some U.S. exporters said the deal involved up to two cargoes.
Soybeans ended six to 1-3/4 cents a bushel higher with July up six at $8.74-1/2. New crop November closed up 5-1/4 at $7.09-3/4 a bushel.

Biedermann said the soybean market held strong despite news more soybeans were being imported into the U.S. "During the selloff we heard Owensboro may be bringing in beans and that's probably true," he said.
Floor sources had mixed opinions on the news, with some terming the deal bearish because it added supply while others said it was an indication that demand was strong enough to merit imports.
New crop months drew strength from evidence the U.S. soybean seeding pace was slower than anticipated and from speculation corn would steal intended acreage from soybeans.

USDA Monday said U.S. soybean seedings as of Sunday were at 20 percent, below trade expectations for up to 25 percent. But the 20 percent pace was well above last year's eight percent completion rate and above the 12 percent average pace.
Corn was 71 percent seeded as of Sunday, well ahead of average. Traders cited talk an analytical firm had cut its forecast for 1997 U.S. soybean acreage.

On the day, funds were on both sides of the market with Refco Inc reportedly a seller of 4.5 million bushels July. Refco also bought 3.5 million July while FIMAT Futures bought 4.5 million November and one million July.
Goldenberg-Hehmeyer spread one million November/July at $1.61-1/2, premium July, and Refco Inc spread 1.2 million November/July at $1.60-1/2 to $1.62.
In options trade, FIMAT bought 1,200 July $8.50 puts and sold 1,200 July $8.25 puts at 9-3/4 to 10 cents. Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 500 November $8.00 calls at 20-1/2.
Soybean futures volume was pegged by CBOT at 73,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 71,826.
